scenario.title: BATTLE OF KURSK - 11 JUL 1943
intro.text:
BATTLE OF KURSK - 11 JUL 1943

South of Kursk, Russia

Despite our prepared defensive positions the Germans continue their advance on Kursk. You will counterattack at Prokhorovka and throw back the Germans before they break through the last lines of defense towards Kursk.

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.

CORE (recommended)
4x Tank
5x Infantry
3x Anti-Tank (+1)
3x Reconnaissance
2x Flak
4x Artillery
4x Fighter Aircraft (+1)
4x Tactical Bomber (+1)
header.act: ACT III — FROM DEFEAT TO OPERATIONAL MASTERY
header.location: Prokhorovka sector, south of Kursk — 11 July 1943
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-briliant.text: The Kharkov defence held every required position and withdrew before the counterstroke could close around it. The city was lost later; the army was not.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-victory.text: The Kharkov approaches were held long enough to blunt the counterattack. We surrendered ground with formations still answering their commanders.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-tactical.text: We got out through a very narrow corridor at Kharkov. Some of those formations are now in the Prokhorovka reserve. They want to see the withdrawal routes before the attack.
line.reaction-lose.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-lose.text: The Kharkov defence failed and the withdrawal routes became separate battles. The formations reassembled at Kursk know prepared lines are valuable because they have just fought without them.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.callback-choice-a.text: The Kharkov men know you meant to hold the approaches. They want to know what would have made you stop. I'd rather you answered than left it to me.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The formations you withdrew from Kharkov are in reserve here. Some officers called them beaten. I can still give them an order and expect a response.
line.scene-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-0.text: The crews can hear the fighting from the assembly areas. Runners keep changing their start positions. If we're waiting for something, tell them what it is.
line.scene-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.scene-1.text: A usable axis. We've paid enough around Kharkov for sending tanks where we couldn't support them. Anna, how much can you confirm before they have to go?
line.decision.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.decision.text: An immediate armoured counterattack may strike before the enemy reorganises. Waiting for artillery and reconnaissance reduces confusion, but the last defensive positions may not survive the delay.
line.decision.choice.counterattack-now.t: Commit the armoured reserve now and seize the initiative at close range.
line.decision.choice.counterattack-now.h: Release an eight-strength T-34/76C detachment with 60 experience and give all tanks 15 experience; emergency commitment costs 120 prestige.
line.decision.choice.coordinate-the-blow: Wait for confirmed axes, artillery preparation, and marked start lines before committing.
Attach an eight-strength 122 mm M-30 battery with 60 experience and give all artillery 15 experience; preparation costs 100 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-0.text: The reserve moves on the current map, not the perfect one. Leading brigades report by radio and the second echelon changes axis if the ground is already blocked.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-1.text: Get a second confirmation before you change axis, Pavel. A wrong first report could turn the whole second echelon onto a blocked road.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-0.text: The start time stands. Reconnaissance and guns use every minute before it so the reserve enters one battle instead of twenty separate collisions.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-b-1.text: I'll wait until that hour. Keep the defensive belt on the radio, though. If the men there can't hold, I want to hear it while we can still help.
line.post-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.post-0.text: Send the agreed start positions to the reserve. Have the runners wait for the commanders to read them this time.
